problem_text:
A logistics coordinator is organizing a shipment of specialized components to a remote research outpost, aiming to maximize the total utility score of the delivered goods while adhering to a strict cargo mass limit.

The components available for selection are:
* Component A: mass 27kg, utility 196 units
* Component B: mass 38kg, utility 64 units
* Component C: mass 6kg, utility 295 units
* Component D: mass 29kg, utility 77 units
* Component E: mass 7kg, utility 17 units
* Component F: mass 34kg, utility 207 units
* Component G: mass 42kg, utility 255 units
* Component H: mass 16kg, utility 211 units
* Component I: mass 41kg, utility 59 units
* Component J: mass 27kg, utility 39 units
* Component K: mass 44kg, utility 161 units
* Component L: mass 39kg, utility 97 units
* Component M: mass 20kg, utility 152 units
* Component N: mass 34kg, utility 73 units
* Component O: mass 36kg, utility 182 units
* Component P: mass 1kg, utility 83 units
* Component Q: mass 1kg, utility 57 units
* Component R: mass 22kg, utility 182 units
* Component S: mass 29kg, utility 111 units

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, exactly one of Component A and Component B must be included in the shipment.

If Component C is selected, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective cargo capacity of the transport vessel by 10 kg.
The vessel can accommodate a maximum total mass of 345 kg. The coordinator must determine the optimal set of components to load.
